spec.claim: The demo-count curve on the SO-101 lift ON THE CLIFF (gain 0.4), with THREE replicates per demo count — three independent presses and training runs each for 8/16/32/64/128 episodes — so the between-run variance that made the single-run curve non-monotone (n8 77/80 vs n16 56/80, 2026-09-03) is measured rather than assumed; comparisons pool the replicates (240 matched trials per count).

n8.basis: declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the folklore DR, docs/31)

n16.basis: declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the folklore DR, docs/31)

n32.basis: declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the folklore DR, docs/31)

n64.basis: declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the folklore DR, docs/31)

n128.basis: declared span ±0.30 around nominal (the folklore DR, docs/31)

caveats: One task, one expert (scripted-pick), one trainer config: the curve is for this recipe, not a law.
Judged at a truth inside the declared span; C1 showed DR-basis effects are invisible at easy truths.

The truth sits where the expert itself succeeds ~1 in 2 (4-trial grid), so the press at the folklore span keeps demos the expert could not repeat at the truth: the referee gates the press at ITS draw, the judge sits at the cliff.
Three replicates per count is the smallest design that shows between-run spread; it is not a variance estimate anyone should quote to two digits.
Fifteen arms: ~6 h of one pod at 10k steps each — split across pods by arm if wall clock matters.
